about.title: About Agios App
about.tagline: "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path" (Ps 119:105)

story.title: Story & Goal
story.p1: The Agios project was launched with a vision to provide a sophisticated digital experience for studying the Bible. It started with participating in the St. Mark Kerygma Festival in Alexandria, where the project sought to provide innovative technical solutions such as advanced linguistic search, interactive maps of holy places, and a modern user interface that helps focus and spiritual growth.
story.p2: After success in the early stages, work continued on developing the platform to become a comprehensive reference that combines daily study tools and modern technical features.

developer.title: About the Developer
developer.desc: The Agios system was developed by Manuel George, a software developer specialized in building innovative web and mobile applications in the service of the Church.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.desc: The vision of Agios is to be a technical bridge connecting generations with the Word of God, using modern tools to present biblical content in an attractive and simplified way, with full commitment to the foundations of the sound Orthodox faith.

thanks.title: Acknowledgements
thanks.priest_desc: We express our deep gratitude and love to {name} for his constant fatherly care for this work from its early moments.
thanks.priest_abraam_desc: We express special appreciation and deep thanks to {name} (General Vicar of the Patriarchate in Alexandria) for his great fatherly support for the application in the early stages of its launch, and his effective help in its dissemination, financing, and providing all material and moral opportunities for the success of this work.
thanks.fcbh: Special thanks to Faith Comes By Hearing for providing the wonderful audio library by Mr. Adel Noshy.
thanks.church: We thank our home church, the Church of the Archangel Michael in Mostafa Kamel - Alexandria, for the continuous support.
thanks.translations: The Van Dyke translation was used for Arabic, the World English Bible for English, the Louis Segond for French, and the Luther for German. All these translations are open source and legally permitted to use.
thanks.general: Special thanks to everyone who contributed by providing technical or spiritual advice.

versions.intro: We are currently in the testing and continuous improvement phase to reach best performance.

history.title: Comprehensive Performance, Design, and AI Improvements

Improvements in Bible display design and book/chapter selection

Improved AI analysis and response speed

fixes: Resolved several bugs and issues reported by users

Improved and developed the badges and points (XP) system to encourage daily interaction
Completed the Book of Esther entirely and added it to the system

Resolved favorite verses synchronization issues across different devices
